Kline, Tyrion's son, played beside him with 6 OPOYs, the most in the league. Pharoah Hunter set the 288-yd game (Y68). The Wilson brothers likely played QB: Wayne (431 games, 90,450 yds, 5 MVPs) and Michael (58,992 yds, 6 MVPs, retired injured mid-season). Combined 11 MVPs and 10 rings.

eras.name: Modern era
eras.notes: Titans three-peat (Y70–72) with Levante Hopkins at tight end and Malakai Sawyer in his one Titans season, then a loss to those same Titans as the Seahawks in CXXXIII (Y74). The Jets, your current club, won CXXXVI (Y77) with Sawyer. Jason Macleone, now a Seahawk, quarterbacked the Vikings to the Y78 title (CXXXVII). Sawyer was traded to the Falcons ahead of Y80.

storylines.headline: 54–6 IN THE BIG GAME
storylines.subheadline: Sixty Super Bowl appearances, Y1 through Y79
storylines.body:
- **54–6 in 60 Super Bowl appearances** across LX–CXXXVIII (CXXVI not captured). You missed 18.
- **20 straight appearances**, LXXIII–XCII (Y14–33), going 18–2.
- **9 straight titles**, LXXXIV–XCII (Y25–33): 2 with the Bucs, then 7 with the Bills.
- **Biggest win:** CXIV (Y55), Giants 68–21 over the Chiefs, the season Brandson threw 94 TDs.
- **Closest wins:** CXXIII (Vikings 40–39 over the Chargers), CXV (Giants 38–37 over the Bills).
- **Losses:** LXVI (Y7, Dolphins to the Commanders), LXXXI and LXXXIII (Y22, Y24, Bucs to McQuay's Colts), CIX (Y50, Ravens to the Saints), CXIX (Y60, Dolphins to the Cowboys), CXXXIII (Y74, Seahawks to the Titans you had just left).
- **Now:** one title (Jets, CXXXVI) in the last seven seasons.
storylines.summary: 54–6 in 60 Super Bowl appearances across LX–CXXXVIII (CXXVI not captured).

storylines.headline: THE RING TAX
storylines.subheadline: What your spreadsheet metrics get wrong
storylines.body:
- **How they work:** Dominance = 0.7 × True Talent + award points (ring 60, MVP 50, OPOY 30, SB MVP 40, DPOY 120, ROTY 0). Career Legacy ≈ 4.6 × Talent + 3.9 × Dominance. TPG ≈ talent per game.
- **Main flaw:** a ring is worth more than an MVP, and every ring went to your team, so the metric rewards being on your roster.
- **Overrated:** Waller (21st in talent, 10th in legacy); dynasty role players Rob Lowe, Deante Elder, Damone Omameh, Taywan Tuttle; Brady (real-life awards); Wayne Wilson (lowest TPG of the elite QBs).
- **Underrated:** Bryant (5th in talent, 13th in legacy); Cooper Dean; Mathieu (17th → 32nd); McQuay; Ikarras (sheet shows 0 OPOY instead of 4, about 470 legacy points short); Baylon (best QB TPG).
- **TPG favors short careers:** Sione 4.95, Perkins 4.79, Benkert 3.27, Jewell 3.41.
- **Suggested fixes:** MVP above ring (e.g. 80 vs 40); DPOY near MVP level; score real-life legends separately; a ~150-game minimum for TPG.
storylines.summary: How they work: Dominance = 0.7 × True Talent + award points (ring 60, MVP 50, OPOY 30, SB MVP 40, DPOY 120, ROTY 0).

storylines.headline: BUILD THE PERFECT PLAYER
storylines.body:
- **QB:** Brandson's accuracy, Waller's deep ball, McQuay's decisions, Bryant's legs, Baylon's clutch, Wayne Wilson's durability.
- **RB:** Sawyer's speed, Ikarras's power and ball security, Hayes's YPC, Gibbs's hands, Inman at the goal line.
- **WR:** God Johnson's volume and hands, Finney's 17.3 yds/catch, Hunter's peak game, Jackson Kline's consistency, Asanjh's MVP impact.
- **Defender:** Queen's coverage, Mose Junior's tackling range, Baugh's pass rush and forced fumbles, Kolar's interior pressure.
storylines.summary: QB: Brandson's accuracy, Waller's deep ball, McQuay's decisions, Bryant's legs, Baylon's clutch, Wayne Wilson's durability.

speeches.Sherman Brandson:
The General never flinched.

Six-foot-seven, built like a tank, and calm enough to put a defense to sleep before he broke its heart. Sherman Brandson stood in the pocket like it belonged to him, and for twenty seasons it did. Pass rushers came in waves and bounced off. Fifty sacks in 315 games. Most quarterbacks give that up in a few bad years.

The numbers read like a typo: 91,463 passing yards, 1,150 touchdown passes, eight MVPs and ten rings, four of them with the Super Bowl MVP trophy in his hands. He looked more like a linebacker than a quarterback, and he played like a man who knew exactly how the next five plays would go.

He did not celebrate much. He did not need to. General Sherman, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
speeches.God Johnson:
He changed his name to God. Then he earned it.

Mason Earl III walked into the league as a receiver. God Johnson walked out as the standard every receiver gets measured against. Some people thought the name was a joke. Defensive coordinators never laughed.

36,005 receiving yards. 378 receiving touchdowns. Ten rings with the Vikings dynasty and five Super Bowl MVPs, because when the lights were brightest the ball found him. And three fumbles. In his entire career. Ian Finney's career receiving mark stood for decades until God took it, with Jackson Wardell Kline lined up beside him.

There is not much left to say about a man who named himself after the only being with a better résumé. God Johnson, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
speeches.Levante Hopkins:
The quiet one who did the dirty work.

Levante Hopkins never looked the part. Glasses off the field, soft-spoken in the locker room, the guy you would mistake for a team analyst. Then he put the helmet on, and nobody in the league wanted to be the one assigned to him.

He played 291 games and caught 1,194 passes for 12,353 yards and 174 touchdowns. He won nine rings and was Super Bowl MVP twice. He was the tight end at the center of the Titans' three-peat from Y70 to Y72: blocking on first down, finding the soft spot on third, and finishing in the red zone.

He never asked for the ball. He just made it hard to lose with him on the field. Levante Hopkins, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
speeches.Ian Finney:
The first superstar. The Infinity Man.

Before the dynasties had names, there was Ian Finney. He was the first player in this league who made you stop what you were doing to watch, the receiver every kid in the backyard pretended to be.

He started with the Commanders' four-peat, then carried the Buccaneers through the Waller–Finney era with Tyrion Kline at his side: nine rings, four in Washington and five in Tampa Bay. He caught 1,902 passes for 32,980 yards and 292 touchdowns at 17.3 yards a catch, and every one of them looked effortless. Add five Offensive Player of the Year awards, an MVP and three Super Bowl MVPs.

Every great receiver who came after him was chasing Ian Finney. Most of them still are. The Infinity Man, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
speeches.Rondale Ikarras:
Flashy, loud, unstoppable, and he knew it. He was that guy.

Rondale Ikarras never just ran through a hole. He ran through it with style, pointed at the crowd, and made sure the cameras got his good side on the way to the end zone. The Prodigal Son played like every snap was a highlight reel, and most of them were.

23,178 rushing yards. 374 rushing touchdowns. Nine rings, four Offensive Player of the Year awards and five Super Bowl MVPs. The career rushing records carry his name. He built a legend in Seattle, three straight titles as the heartbeat of the Seahawks, and took one last ride with the Jets before hanging it up.

Zero regular-season MVPs. He will tell you about that one. Rondale Ikarras, Seahawks legend, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
